claim: Endothelial YAP and TAZ repress Notch and BMP signalling during angiogenesis and retinal vascular expansion.

claim: Treatment with the Notch inhibitor DBZ corrects the Notch reporter activity increase after YAP and TAZ knockdown in HUVECs.
source: Treatment with the Notch inhibitor DBZ corrected the Notch reporter activity increase after YAP and TAZ knockdown in HUVECs (Figure 8A)
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8A

claim: Treatment with the Notch inhibitor DBZ does not affect the migration of YAP/TAZ knockdown cells in the scratch wound assay.
source: but did not affect the migration of cells in the scratch wound assay (Figure 8B)
evidence: Supported by scratch-wound assay data shown in Figure 8B

claim: Only Ldn193187, an Alk2/3/1 kinase inhibitor, significantly decreases the BMP reporter activity after YAP and TAZ knockdown.

evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 8D

claim: Ldn193187 treatment partially rescues the migration defect of YAP/TAZ knockdown HUVECs in the scratch wound assay.
source: Ldn193187 treatment partially rescued the migration defect of YAP/TAZ knockdown HUVECs in the scratch wound assay, significantly increasing the wound closure at 16 hr from 33 ± 3% in DMSO treated cells to 56 ± 5% in Ldn193187 treated cells (p=0.0022) (Figure 8E)
evidence: Supported by scratch-wound assay data shown in Figure 8E

claim: Ldn193187 treatment fully rescues the permeability defect of YAP/TAZ knockdown HUVECs to 250 kDa FITC dextran molecules.
source: Ldn193187 treatment fully rescued the permeability defect of YAP/TAZ knockdown HUVECs to 250 kDa FITC dextran molecules (Figure 8F)
evidence: Supported by permeability assay data shown in Figure 8F

claim: Ldn193187 treatment decreases the frequency of finger junctions in YAP/TAZ deficient cells to the levels found in control cells.
source: Quantification of junction morphologies identified that Ldn193187 treatment decreased the frequency of finger junctions in YAP/TAZ deficient cells to the levels found in control cells (Figure 8I and Figure 5F, % of fingers: siYAP/TAZ DMSO, 25 ± 5%, siYAP/TAZ Ldn193187 12 ± 0.6%, siCTR: 9 ± 4%)

claim: Ldn193187 treatment leads to a 3-fold increase in thick to reticular and reticular junctions in YAP/TAZ knockdown cells.

claim: The BMP signaling increase is at least partially involved in the cellular defects caused by YAP/TAZ deficiency.
source: Together, these results show that the BMP signaling increase is at least partially involved in the cellular defects caused by YAP/TAZ deficiency.

claim: Forced activation of YAP and TAZ leads to increased expression of the BMP ligands BMP2, BMP4 and BMP6.
source: Forced activation of YAP and TAZ led to increased expression of the BMP ligands BMP2, BMP4 and BMP6, which cannot explain the increase in BMP signalling in the loss of function condition.

claim: Forced activation of YAP and TAZ leads to increased expression of the BMP antagonists FST, CTGF, BAMBI, SMURF2, NOG and SMURF1.
source: However, we also found increased expression of the BMP antagonists FST, CTGF, BAMBI, SMURF2, NOG and SMURF1.

claim: YAP and TAZ decrease BMP signalling in endothelial cells possibly by increasing the expression of BMP inhibitors.
source: Thus YAP and TAZ decrease BMP signalling in endothelial cells possibly by increasing the expression of BMP inhibitors.
evidence: Inferred from gene expression analysis of BMP pathway components

claim: YAP/TAZ repress BMP activation in endothelial cells, modulating junctions and cell migration.
source: Together, these results suggest that YAP/TAZ repress BMP activation in endothelial cells, modulating junctions and cell migration.
evidence: Inferred from BMP inhibition rescue experiments and gene expression data

claim: YAP and TAZ show distinct expression patterns in endothelial cells, although these proteins show a high degree of redundancy in many other cell types.
source: Our finding that YAP and TAZ were present in the nucleus of ECs at the sprouting front of developing vessels shows parallels with other cell types where nuclear YAP and TAZ are detected in actively proliferating areas of developing tissues. Interestingly, however, YAP and TAZ show distinct expression patterns in ECs, although these proteins show a high degree of redundancy in many other cell types.
evidence: Based on observed expression patterns and comparison to other cell types

claim: Cytoplasmic YAP promotes endothelial cell migration.
source: Interestingly, recent work by Sakabe and colleagues showed that cytoplasmic YAP promotes endothelial cell migration (Sakabe et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: Endothelial YAP associates with adherens junction proteins at stable junctions and this prevents its nuclear accumulation and transcriptional activity.
source: A previous study by Giampietro and colleagues (Giampietro et al., 2015) has shown that endothelial YAP associates with adherens junction proteins at stable junctions and that this prevents its nuclear accumulation and transcriptional activity.
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: Endothelial cells at the sprouting front display reduced relative VE-Cadherin concentration that promotes cell-cell junction dynamics and JAIL formation.
source: In the mouse retina vasculature, Cao and colleagues (Cao et al., 2017) recently observed that endothelial cells at the sprouting front display reduced relative VE-Cadherin concentration that promotes cell-cell junction dynamics and JAIL formation.
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: Reduced VE-Cadherin concentration at cell junctions may promote YAP and TAZ relocation to the nucleus.
source: Together, these data provide additional strength to a model in which reduced VE-Cadherin concentration at cell junctions may promote YAP and TAZ relocation to the nucleus.
evidence: Inferred from cited literature and observed expression patterns

claim: In zebrafish, YAP nuclear relocation correlates with lumenisation of sprouting vessels.
source: In zebrafish, Nakajima and colleagues (Nakajima et al., 2017) showed that YAP nuclear relocation correlated with lumenisation of sprouting vessels, and they attributed this to the effect of shear stress on YAP.
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: In the mouse retina, hemodynamic fluid laws predict that vessels at the sprouting front experience very low levels of shear.
source: In the mouse retina, hemodynamic fluid laws predict that vessels at the sprouting front experience very low levels of shear (Bernabeu et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: YAP and TAZ do not respond to 12 or 24 hr of laminar shear.
source: In support of this idea, YAP and TAZ appear not to respond to 12 or 24 hr of laminar shear (Wang et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: YAP and TAZ translocate to the nucleus after only 10 min of laminar shear.
source: but translocate to the nucleus after only 10 min of laminar shear (Nakajima et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: The mild phenotype of the single mutants in comparison to the drastic phenotype of the compound mutant indicates functional redundancy in the endothelium.
source: The mild phenotype of the single mutants in comparison to the drastic phenotype of the compound mutant indicates functional redundancy in the endothelium.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of single and double mutant phenotypes

claim: Endothelial YAP/TAZ signalling is critically involved in ensuring adequate endothelial cell distribution.
source: However, our further discovery that YAP and TAZ are required to establish homogeneity in the plexus and prevent cellular aggregations suggests that endothelial YAP/TAZ signalling is not only required to provide adequate numbers of cells but is also critically involved in ensuring adequate EC distribution.
evidence: Inferred from observed phenotypes in loss-of-function models

claim: Endothelial YAP/TAZ provide a cell intrinsic mechanism of locally controlling cell densities, in contrast to growth factor-mediated cell proliferation instructed by the surrounding tissue.
source: We propose that in this way endothelial YAP/TAZ provide a cell intrinsic mechanism of locally controlling cell densities, in contrast to growth factor-mediated cell proliferation instructed by the surrounding tissue.
evidence: Proposed model based on experimental findings

claim: Endothelial YAP/TAZ increase VE-Cadherin turnover at cell-cell junctions, which is essential for cells to migrate and rearrange while maintaining the endothelial barrier.
source: Second, endothelial YAP/TAZ increase VE-Cadherin turnover at cell-cell junctions, which we propose is essential for cells to migrate and rearrange while maintaining the endothelial barrier at the same time.
evidence: Proposed model based on experimental findings

claim: YAP regulates hepatocyte adherens junctions in response to increased actomyosin contractility by increasing myosin II light chain gene expression.
source: This corroborates recent findings in mouse hepatocytes where YAP antagonises adherens junction stability (Bai et al., 2016). The authors showed that YAP regulates hepatocyte adherens junctions in response to increased actomyosin contractility by increasing myosin II light chain gene expression.
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: The transcriptional, nuclear role of YAP is required for junctional regulation in hepatocytes.
source: Accordingly, the transcriptional, nuclear role of YAP was required for junctional regulation.
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: There exists a positive feedback loop where stable junctions sequester YAP and TAZ from the nucleus, maintaining less junctional turnover, while remodelling junctions allow YAP and TAZ to relocate to the nucleus where they increase VE-Cadherin turnover.
source: Together with our observations, these findings indicate the existence of a positive feedback loop where stable junctions sequester YAP and TAZ from the nucleus, therefore maintaining less junctional turnover, while remodelling junctions allow YAP and TAZ to relocate to the nucleus where they increase VE-Cadherin turnover.
evidence: Proposed model based on experimental findings and cited literature

claim: A high VE-Cadherin turnover at the sprouting front is required to maintain junctional integrity and prevent bleedings.
source: Our results also suggest that a high VE-Cadherin turnover at the sprouting front is required in order to maintain junctional integrity and prevent bleedings.
evidence: Inferred from observed phenotypes in loss-of-function models

claim: YAP and TAZ increase Cdc42 activity in lamellipodia and phosphorylation of N-WASP.
source: These results are in accordance with recent data from Sakabe and colleagues reporting that YAP and TAZ increase Cdc42 activity in lamellipodia and phosphorylation of N-WASP (Sakabe et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: N-WASP is an actin binding protein that promotes branching of actin through the activation of the Arp2/3 complex.
source: an actin binding protein that promotes branching of actin through the activation of the Arp2/3 complex.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge

source: This is further corroborated by in vivo data from Kim and colleagues showing that DAPT treatment fails to restore sprouting defects in YAP/TAZ mutant retinas (Kim et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: BMP9/10 – Alk1 signalling is anti-angiogenic.
source: Previous studies identified that BMP9/10 – Alk1 signalling is anti-angiogenic (Larrivée et al., 2012)
evidence: Supported by cited literature

claim: BMP2/4/6 - Alk2/Alk3 signalling is pro-angiogenic.
source: while BMP2/4/6 - Alk2/Alk3 signalling is pro-angiogenic (Lee et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by cited literature

source: Together, our results identify a role for YAP/TAZ in promoting endothelial cellular rearrangements through the regulation of junctional turnover and collectiveness of cell migration.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings

claim: Linking stretch-induced proliferation with modulation of junctional turnover is ideally suited to achieve the required balance of cell distribution for functional vascular patterning.
source: Conceptually, linking stretch-induced proliferation (to balance cell numbers) with modulation of junctional turnover (to facilitate cell rearrangements) seems ideally suited to achieve the required balance of cell distribution for functional vascular patterning.
evidence: Conceptual interpretation of experimental findings
